rules.title: Type-parameter method dispatch via trait bound
rules.statement: A method call `t.m(args)` where `t : T` (T a type parameter) resolves `m` only if some in-scope bound `T: Trait` (or supertrait reference) declares a method named `m`; the chosen trait/method drive the call. If no in-scope bound on T provides `m` and no Deref/DerefMut bound applies, it is an error: "type parameter '<T>' has no trait bound providing method '<m>'".

rules.title: Substitute Self and trait type-params from the receiver bound
rules.statement: When dispatching a trait method on receiver of type T, the substitution binds `Self := T` and binds each trait type-parameter to the matching concrete type-argument from the in-scope bound `T: Trait<A0,A1,...>` (positional pairing, type_params[i] := type_args[i] when present). The method return type is computed by applying this substitution.

rules.title: Lifetime substitution by structural pairing of method formals vs actuals
rules.statement: Lifetime parameters of a dispatched method are substituted by structurally walking each formal parameter type against its actual argument type (receiver vs param0, then arg[i] vs param[i+1]): for matching Ref/MutRef pairs the formal lifetime maps to the actual lifetime and the walk recurses into pointees; for matching nominal types (Struct/ZonedStruct/Enum) lifetime-args are paired positionally. First binding wins per formal lifetime.

rules.title: Associated-type return projection carries the bound's concrete trait type-args
rules.statement: If a dispatched trait method's substituted return type is an associated-type projection, its trait name is rewritten to the trait-name suffixed with the bound's concrete trait type-args (`Trait<...>` -> mangled args suffix), so projections from two distinct `impl Trait<T>` for one type, and the caller's declared `-> P::Item`, resolve to the same impl.
rules.uncertainty: Disambiguation among multiple Trait<T> impls; tied to G156-1 trait-type-arg mangling (still narrow per memory).

rules.title: Auto-ref of receiver to match &self / &mut self
rules.statement: If the dispatched method's first formal is a reference (`&self`/`&mut self`) and the receiver value is neither a reference nor a raw pointer, the receiver is implicitly wrapped in an address-of (`&` or `&mut` per the formal's mutability) producing a reference-typed receiver.

rules.title: Trait-qualified method symbol when a method name is provided by a trait
rules.statement: When at least one trait declares a method of the given name, the call is tagged with the chosen trait so monomorphization may resolve the trait-qualified symbol `<Concrete>__<Trait>__<method>`; mono falls back to the plain name when no qualified symbol exists. This disambiguates multi-trait collisions and cases where a same-named inherent method occupies the plain symbol.

rules.title: Trait tag folds concrete bound type-args into a $G<n>$ suffix
rules.statement: When the receiver bound carries concrete trait type-args (`T: MyTrait<u64>`), the trait tag becomes `Trait` + `$G<n>$<args>` suffix, so mono resolves the args-qualified symbol `<Concrete>__MyTrait$G1$u64__method`, distinct from a sibling `impl MyTrait<u8>`.

rules.title: Propagate trait-level then method-level type-args to the call
rules.statement: The lowered method call carries type-args in order: first each owning-trait type-parameter (bound from the Self-substitution), then each method-level type-parameter inferred by unifying substituted formal param types against actual argument types. Unbound positions are left null.

rules.title: Autoderef through a Deref/DerefMut bound when no bound provides the method
rules.statement: If no in-scope bound on type-parameter T provides method `m`, but T has a bound `T: Deref<C>` (or `DerefMut<C>`), the receiver is rewritten to `recv.deref()` (resp. `deref_mut()`), typed `&C` (resp. `&mut C`), and method resolution falls through to the ordinary inherent/struct-method path on C.

rules.title: Receiver reference stripped to its pointee for nominal method lookup
rules.statement: For method-formal hinting and dispatch, a receiver of reference type (`&T`/`&mut T`) is reduced to its pointee T before extracting the struct/enum name and binding the receiver's nominal type-arguments into the substitution.

rules.title: Receiver nominal type-args bound into method formal substitution
rules.statement: When the receiver is a generic Struct/ZonedStruct or Enum carrying type-args, the nominal type's declared type-parameters are bound positionally to those args; this substitution is applied to the method's formal parameter types when computing argument type hints.

rules.title: Owning-trait type-params bound from the receiver's impl
rules.statement: For a method belonging to a trait, the trait's type-parameters (e.g. `Iterator<Item>`) are bound from the receiver type's `impl Trait for Recv` trait-type-args (positional, only filling names not already bound by the receiver's own type-args), so Fn-family bound argument types resolve concretely for closure-formal hints.

rules.title: Turbofish binds method-level type-params in order, skipping already-bound
rules.statement: An explicit turbofish on a method call (`it.fold::<i32>(..)`) provides the method-level type-arguments in order; each is bound to the next method type-parameter not already bound by the receiver substitution (struct-inherited params bound from the receiver are skipped).

rules.title: Closure/literal argument types hinted from method formal parameter
rules.statement: Each argument is lowered with a type hint derived from the corresponding method formal: a single Ref/MutRef wrapper on the formal is stripped, then a function/closure formal seeds the closure hint, a generic Enum/Struct (with type-args) seeds the enum/struct hint, and a Tuple formal seeds the tuple hint. An Fn-family-bounded bare type-parameter formal synthesizes a Closure hint from the bound's signature so an untyped closure (`|i|`) infers its parameter types.

rules.title: Method-call argument list shape depends on turbofish presence
rules.statement: A method call without turbofish carries its arguments as a flat array under ARGS; a turbofish method call wraps the arguments as `{ ITEMS: [...] }` (mirroring generic/static calls).

rules.title: Generic-enum method dispatch instantiates the method template
rules.statement: For a receiver of generic Enum type (`Enum<...>` with type-args) whose method is a generic template, dispatch routes through the generic-call path with type-args = receiver enum type-args (struct-level prefix) followed by inferred or turbofish-supplied method-level type-args; the receiver's enum type-params are pre-seeded into the substitution before inference.

rules.title: Calling an unsafe method requires an unsafe context
rules.statement: A call to a method marked unsafe outside an unsafe context is an error: "call to unsafe method '<name>' requires unsafe context".

rules.title: Primitive-receiver methods resolved via TypeName__method with receiver-shape variants
rules.statement: For a receiver with no struct name, the method is looked up as `<type-name>__<method>` matched against the actual argument signature; if no direct match, receiver-shape variants are tried in order: `&T`, `&mut T`, `*const T`, `*mut T`, and (for reference receivers) the `$ref_<...>` / `$mut_ref_<...>` mangling used to register `impl Trait for &T` / `&mut T`.
